paragraphs.text: Thirteen , in folklore, is an unlucky number in superstition, though its source is disputed as well as its recency. As part of the Gothic Horror theme of Innistrad , the designers wove in recurring references to the number on cards, which also proved to be a design challenge due to the magnitude of the number.

During the design of Innistrad , designer Jenna Helland turned in a ten-damage creature removal spell which would later become Into the Maw of Hell . Mark Rosewater suggested that ten could be thirteen as an unlucky number, which received positive reception amongst the team. From then on, there was a desire to have effects that referenced 13 wherever possible. For example, Tragic Slip , a card that would normally have been "destroy target creature" when Morbid was active, instead was made to give −13/−13; functionally very similar but incorporated the motif.

This motif continued whenever Innistrad was returned to, sometimes bringing new designs or referencing previous designs. Of the 47 cards that have thirteen on them, 29 of them were printed in blocks featuring Innistrad or referenced cards from Innistrad. This includes sets like March of the Machine , Magic: The Gathering Foundations and Jumpstart 2022 , which are plane-neutral. Ten of the remainder are the unlucky lands , a double cycle from another horror plane Duskmourn .

The magnitude of the number made for a challenge, as few things could be set to 13 without being unappealing to cost or having diminishing returns. Only so many creatures can be made with 13 power or toughness, and many lower rarity spells that use 13 amount to being removal spells.
Some spells have a lineage of cards that reference them:
Tragic Slip Tragic Fall Tragic Banshee Olivia's Midnight Ambush Tragic Trajectory
Tree of Redemption Tree of Perdition Disciple of Perdition
Blasphemous Act Blasphemous Edict Vanquish the Horde
Two cards from the Doctor Who set reference thirteen as the number of iterations of The Doctor that were present at that point in the series continuity.
Three cards were printed before Innistrad block that had 13 in their text or stat line, but none were part of any concerted effort.
